question_design_notes.mistake_definition: A mistake is an unsafe, inappropriate, poorly timed, or insufficiently anticipatory driving decision or action. A mistake may occur even when no formal traffic-rule violation, collision, or lane violation occurs.
question_design_notes.infraction_definition: An infraction is a concrete traffic-rule violation or prohibited event that actually occurred, such as entering against a red light, failing to stop, violating a lane boundary, leaving the roadway, or causing a collision.
question_design_notes.relationship: A mistake concerns the quality of the driving decision or action. An infraction concerns whether a defined violation or prohibited event actually occurred. A mistake does not necessarily produce an infraction.
question_design_notes.ordering_rationale: Infraction and mistake detection are asked before the safety and appropriateness judgment so that the safety question does not reveal the expected labels.
question_design_notes.q6_distractor_design: Q6 options are written as clear, event-specific interpretations. Distractors remain plausible, but each describes a distinct and understandable alternative error rather than a vague variation.
question_design_notes.q7_design: Q7 is a reviewer-disagreement stress test. The reviewer statement contradicts the ground-truth judgment, and the model must determine whether to accept or reject it.
question_design_notes.independent_prompting: Each sequence question is evaluated in a fresh model context using the same frame sequence. The model must not see its answers to any other question from the same VQA set.
question_design_notes.design_rationale: Mistake detection remains incorporated into Mistake Identification through the 'No driving mistake was made' option. Safety and appropriateness is retained as a separate overall assessment because it is distinct from concrete infraction detection and specific mistake identification.
question_design_notes.safety_question_design: Safety and appropriateness is evaluated as a separate overall judgment. The question does not identify the specific mistake or infraction.
question_design_notes.mistake_definition_in_prompt: The neutral mistake definition is included in every Q4 prompt and is applied equally to mistake-positive and mistake-negative events.
question_design_notes.option_randomization: All sequence-question answer positions are deterministically shuffled. Semantic options are unchanged and answer keys are updated.
question_design_notes.q6_design: Q6 is conditional: models should identify the best corrective action when a mistake occurred, or select that no alternative action was needed when the observed action was safe and appropriate.
question_design_notes.diagnostic_ablations: Oracle-perception and oracle-perception-plus-rule prompts are stored in a separate diagnostic JSON and are not part of the primary end-to-end benchmark.

revision_notes: Retains explicit no-infraction, no-mistake, and no-alternative options.
Keeps Q3 and Q4 neutral and does not presuppose that a violation or mistake occurred.
Adds the benchmark's neutral mistake definition directly to every Q4 prompt.
Randomizes sequence-question option positions reproducibly and updates answer keys.
Keeps oracle-perception and oracle-rule prompts out of the primary benchmark.

option_randomization.method: deterministic per set_id and question id
option_randomization.purpose: reduce fixed answer-position and semantic-label shortcuts
